**B01AE07** is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for dabigatran, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src1] [^src3]. Within the Danish healthcare system, this specific drug code is systematically tracked to measure the quality of care for patients with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1] [^src3]. Specifically, B01AE07 is monitored as part of the national clinical quality indicators for both [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] and the requisite kidney function monitoring for these patients [^src4] [^src5].

The code is a central component of the data infrastructure managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut). In the annual "Atrieflimren i Danmark" (Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark) reports spanning 2023 to 2025, B01AE07 is explicitly defined alongside other key pharmacological codes to ensure standardized data collection and comparison across Danish regions [^src1] [^src2] [^src4]. 

According to the technical specifications for these quality indicators, oral [[antikoagulationsbehandling|anticoagulation treatment]] encompasses [[b01aa|B01AA]] (vitamin K antagonists) as well as the DOACs: B01AE07 (dabigatran), [[b01af01|B01AF01]] (rivaroxaban), [[b01af02|B01AF02]] (apixaban), and [[b01af03|B01AF03]] (edoxaban) [^src1] [^src5]. By precisely defining B01AE07 and its related codes, the national registry can accurately calculate denominators and numerators for treatment indicators, ensuring evidence-based clinical standards are met in the treatment of cardiovascular disease [^src2] [^src3].
